name: Duck Buffath
subtitle: duck stewed with vinegar and whole spice, a Christmas table dish

ingredients.note: buffath is a vinegar stew; this is not a place to economise

prepNotes: Buffath is close kin to Goan vindaloo and sorpotel: meat, vinegar, garlic and long keeping. It sat on Anglo-Indian Christmas tables because it improved for days.
Render the duck fat off first and cook the onions in it. Nothing else gives the same depth.

steps.text: Brown the duck pieces skin down in a dry heavy pot until the fat runs and the skin is deep gold. Lift out.
steps.tip: No oil. There is more than enough fat in the bird.

steps.text: Pour off all but 4 tbsp of the fat. Fry the onions in it until soft and brown, 15 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chillies, cinnamon, cloves, pepper and turmeric. Fry 3 minutes.
Return the duck, add the vinegar and 400ml water, cover and simmer 70 minutes until the meat pulls easily.
Add the potato for the last 25 minutes. Season with salt and the sugar.
steps.tip: The sugar is not for sweetness, it takes the raw edge off the vinegar.

steps.text: Rest overnight if you can. It is a better dish on day two.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and genuinely improves for the first two, which is the vinegar doing its work. Reheat to a full simmer. Freezes for a month.
